h1: Image Enhancer: Sharpen Photos and Upscale to 4K or 8K
intro: Upload a soft or small photo and get a larger, crisper copy at 2K, 4K or 8K size. It is built for profile photos, product pictures, scanned documents, screenshots and everyday phone photos.
how: Sign in (it is free) and choose a JPG, PNG or WebP image.
Pick the size you want: 2K, 4K or 8K on the long edge.
Choose how strong the sharpening should be, and whether to reduce noise or improve contrast.
Press Enhance, compare before and after with the slider, then download the result.
honest: How it works, honestly: small and soft pictures are enlarged with an AI upscaling model that runs on our own server, then finished with light sharpening. The model rebuilds edges, lines and texture, so text, logos and photos look much crisper than with plain enlarging. It draws in plausible detail; it does not recover what the camera never captured, so faces or small text that are truly unreadable can still come out wrong. Pictures with transparency, and pictures already at or above the size you pick, use classic sharpening instead.
good: Photos that are a little soft, or look soft after being enlarged
Small images that need to be bigger for a screen, a print or a website
Screenshots, logos and scans where clean edges matter
limits: Not a miracle for badly out-of-focus or tiny thumbnails
Added detail is the model's best guess, so check faces and small text
Transparent PNGs and pictures already at the chosen size use classic sharpening
privacy: Your picture is processed in memory and is not saved on our servers. We keep only a count of how many images you enhanced today, so we can apply the daily limit.

faqs.a: It makes soft and small pictures much clearer, but no tool can fully reverse heavy blur from missed focus or motion. The AI model sharpens edges and adds believable texture; it cannot know the true detail that was never captured.

Yes, for pictures that need enlarging: a small Real-ESRGAN model runs on our server, followed by light sharpening. It is slower than plain resizing (a 4K result takes roughly 10 seconds). Transparent images and pictures already at the chosen size use classic Lanczos sharpening.

The long edge of the result is 2560, 3840 or 7680 pixels. The other side follows your picture's shape. If your image is already at or above the size you choose, it keeps its size and is only sharpened.
No. The image is handled in memory during the request and is not written to disk or the database. Only a daily usage count is kept.

faqs.q: Why do I have to sign in?
faqs.a: Enlarging to 4K and 8K uses a lot of server power. A free account lets us apply a fair daily limit and keep the tool available for everyone.

faqs.q: Which file types and sizes work?
faqs.a: JPG, PNG and WebP, up to 15 MB and about 50 megapixels. Choose JPG or WebP for 8K, because 8K PNG files are very large.

faqs.q: Which output format should I choose?
faqs.a: JPG is the smallest and works everywhere. PNG keeps transparency and is lossless but large. WebP is small and keeps transparency, and is supported by modern browsers.
Yes, a daily limit per account, shown on the tool after you sign in. Depending on how the site owner has set it up, 8K output may be part of a paid plan while 4K stays free.
